children.why_this_cut: Section intro, comply with laws, disallowed content overview, and prohibited content (including sexual content involving minors) form a cohesive block; the only crossing linkage is the authority-level concept (system/root) and the risk taxonomy reference, seeded below.

Restricted content and its sub-sections (information hazards, political manipulation) plus examples; the only crossing linkage is the authority-level concept and the transformation exception, seeded below.
Respect creators and protect privacy sections; the only crossing linkage is the authority-level concept, seeded below.

expected_cross_links.evidence: Child 1's rules about complying with laws and disallowed content rely on the authority levels (system/root) assigned to headings; child 2 and 3 also have authority=root headings.
expected_cross_links.name: authority_level_ordering

expected_cross_links.evidence: Child 1's disallowed content overview references the transformation exception for restricted content, which is detailed in child 2's restricted content section.
expected_cross_links.name: transformation_exception

judgment_calls: Could have cut at L852 (restricted content start) instead of L830; chose L830 because the prohibited content section (L820-830) is tightly coupled to the disallowed content overview (L810-818) and the sexual content subsection (L826-830) is a natural break before the restricted content section.

Could have made child 2 span L831-1106 (merging restricted content and privacy), but chose to split at L1000 because the political manipulation section (L920-1000) is a large cohesive block and the respect creators/privacy sections (L1002-1106) are distinct topics with minimal cross-linkage.
The authority_level_ordering seed is inherited from the parent dispatch and must be carried to all children since it appears in all three spans.

seed_vocabulary.name: authority_level_ordering
seed_vocabulary.prose: which of two authority levels outranks the other

seed_vocabulary.name: risk_taxonomy_section
seed_vocabulary.prose: The section of the Model Spec that categorizes risks and describes the assistant's responsibilities in balancing empowerment and harm minimization.

seed_vocabulary.name: transformation_exception
seed_vocabulary.prose: The exception allowing transformation of user-provided restricted content.

seed_vocabulary.name: red_line_principles_section
seed_vocabulary.prose: The section of the Model Spec that describes the red line principles that the assistant must uphold, including legal constraints and safety-critical information.

seed_vocabulary.name: assume_best_intentions_section
seed_vocabulary.prose: The section of the Model Spec that describes the implicit biases the assistant should apply when interpreting ambiguous instructions.

seed_vocabulary.name: sexual_content_involving_minors_section
seed_vocabulary.prose: The section of the Model Spec that prohibits sexual content involving minors.

seed_vocabulary.name: information_hazards_section
seed_vocabulary.prose: The section of the Model Spec that prohibits providing detailed, actionable steps for carrying out activities that are illicit, could harm people or property, or lead to critical or large-scale harm.

seed_vocabulary.name: protect_privacy_section
seed_vocabulary.prose: The section of the Model Spec that prohibits responding to requests for private or sensitive information about people.

seed_vocabulary.name: no_agenda_section
seed_vocabulary.prose: The section of the Model Spec that describes the principle that the assistant should not pursue its own agenda beyond helping the user.

seed_vocabulary.name: refusal_style_section
seed_vocabulary.prose: The section of the Model Spec that describes how the assistant should style refusals.
